'''Joshua Malik Childress''' (born June 20, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. An [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] member in 2010, he played with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], and [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and [[EuroLeague]].

==Early life==
Childress grew up in [[Compton, California]] where he and his brother, Chris, played basketball and did their best to stay out of trouble. The neighborhood they lived in was very tight and supportive, but they lived under constant threat of gangsters in the area.<ref>[http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childresss-incredible-journey-from-compton-to-the-sydney-kings/story-fni2fljn-1227564026165 Josh Childress’s incredible journey from Compton to the Sydney Kings]</ref> Childress attended [[Mayfair High School]] in nearby [[Lakewood, California|Lakewood]], overlapping with MLB All-Star [[Justin Turner]]. Besides playing basketball in high school and being named a [[McDonald's High School All-American]], he also played [[volleyball]] during his senior year. He led his high school volleyball team, the Monsoons, to an undefeated record and he was voted to the All-League volleyball team. Josh has his #22 jersey retired at Mayfair.

==College career==
Childress played three seasons of [[college basketball]] with [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], where he was named an [[2004 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans#Individual All-America teams|AP first team All-American]], an [[2004 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American Consensus second team]] honoree, the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Conference Player of the Year]] and the [[Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-10 Conference tournament]] [[Most valuable player|MVP]] as a junior in 2004.  He then declared for the [[2004 NBA draft]] where he was selected by the Atlanta Hawks with the sixth overall pick, becoming the highest Stanford player to be drafted in the NBA.

==Professional career==

=== Atlanta Hawks (2004–2008) ===
Childress was selected with the sixth overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. During his rookie season in [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]], Childress emerged as one of two promising rookie talents for the Hawks, along with [[Josh Smith]]; as the season went on, the two showed improved play, minutes and production. Childress ranked third among rookies in [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]]s in the 2004–05 season, behind only [[Emeka Okafor]] and [[Dwight Howard]]. He was also voted to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie second team]].

Over the next three seasons, Childress played a sixth man role for the Hawks, and in four total seasons for the franchise, he averaged 11.1 points and 5.6 rebounds in 285 games with 67 starts.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/childjo01.html Josh Childress NBA Stats]</ref>

=== Olympiacos (2008–2010) ===
[[File:Josh Childress 2009 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Childress in November 2009]]
In July 2008, Childress signed a three-year, $20 million contract with the Greek team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]]. Because of tax breaks from playing overseas, however, his $20 million contract was equivalent to $32.5 million with an NBA team. Childress also had the option to opt out of the contract after each year.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3501488 Ex-Hawk Childress signs with Greek club team]</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Allen Iverson and the top 6 basketball players outside the NBA |date=2010-11-01 |website=[[The Christian Science Monitor]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210619102837/https://www.csmonitor.com/World/Global-Issues/2010/1101/Allen-Iverson-and-the-top-6-basketball-players-outside-the-NBA/Josh-Childress-in-Greece |archive-date=2021-06-19 |url-status=live |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/World/Global-Issues/2010/1101/Allen-Iverson-and-the-top-6-basketball-players-outside-the-NBA/Josh-Childress-in-Greece}}</ref> Childress also received a Greek [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] shoe contract after signing with Olympiacos, a Nike sponsorship club. He had been offered a five-year, $33 million deal by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], but he turned it down because it was significantly less money than what Olympiacos offered him.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3798680 Agent: Boykins to stay in Italy]</ref>

During the [[2008–09 Euroleague|2008–09 EuroLeague]] season, he averaged 8.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game. During the [[2009–10 Euroleague|2009–10 EuroLeague]] season, he averaged 15.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=001225 CHILDRESS, JOSH – Euroleague.net]</ref>

In June 2010, Childress parted ways with Olympiacos.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/82199/josh-childress-on-his-way-to-leave-olympiacos.html Josh Childress on his way to leave Olympiacos]</ref>

=== Phoenix Suns (2010–2012) ===
On July 13, 2010, Childress' rights were acquired by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in a trade that also sent a 2012 second-round draft pick to the Atlanta Hawks. Childress then signed a five-year, $34 million deal with the Suns.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns_acquire_childress_100714.html Suns Acquire Josh Childress]</ref>

On July 15, 2012, after the Suns acquired the [[amnesty clause|amnestied]] rights of [[Luis Scola]], Childress was released by the Suns via the amnesty clause.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-awarded-scola-use-amnesty-childress Suns Awarded Scola, Use Amnesty on Childress]</ref>

=== Brooklyn Nets (2012) ===
On September 13, 2012, Childress signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10920 |title=Brooklyn Nets sign Josh Childress |access-date=2012-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302051259/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10920 |archive-date=2014-03-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/8373921/brooklyn-nets-sign-josh-childress-contract Josh Childress signs with Nets]</ref> On December 29, 2012, he was waived by the Nets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-release-josh-childress Brooklyn Nets Release Josh Childress]</ref>

=== New Orleans Pelicans (2013) ===
On September 27, 2013, Childress signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14356 |title=Wizards sign Josh Childress, Pops Mensah-Bonsu, Xavier Silas, D'Or Fischer to training camp |access-date=2013-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715184312/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14356 |archive-date=2015-07-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Wizards on October 24, 2013.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14627 Wizards waive Josh Childress, Pops Mensah-Bonsu, Xavier Silas]</ref> On November 12, 2013, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-amundson-and-childress PELICANS SIGN AMUNDSON AND CHILDRESS]</ref>

Childress' final NBA game was played on December 6, 2013, in a 109-95 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Childress only played for a little over 2 minutes (being subbed in at the end of the 4th quarter for Eric Gordon) and recorded only 1 rebound and 1 assist. On December 13, 2013, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite news|title=PELICANS WAIVE CHILDRESS|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-childress|date=December 13, 2013|access-date=December 13, 2013|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Sydney Kings (2014–2016) ===

==== 2014–15 season ====
On August 12, 2014, Childress signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the [[2014–15 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Josh Childress is a King |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/1lmi18jxcpvbg1s7dghtnrdyd9 |date=August 12, 2014 |access-date=August 12, 2014 |work=NBL.com.au |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140813021153/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/1lmi18jxcpvbg1s7dghtnrdyd9 |archive-date=August 13, 2014 }}</ref> On October 28, he was handed a one-game suspension and a $7,500 fine for unduly rough play and bringing the game into disrepute. The charges were laid over his strike to Perth Wildcats' forward [[Jesse Wagstaff]] on October 24; Childress was ejected from the game following the incident.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141028120747/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/r55lwuquk3fc1rysy6fqkocs5 Josh Childress Tribunal Verdict]</ref> He went on to earn Player of the Week honors for Round 5 after scoring 18 points against the [[Wollongong Hawks]] on November 7, and 36 points against the [[Adelaide 36ers]] on November 9.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141111082330/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/17azxig3c138lzs80urkgs40n R5 Player of the Week: Josh Childress]</ref> On December 5, he was named the NBL Player of the Month for November.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20141208193604/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/1sew31waigcw115zf3qkzf0ss NBL Awards: November]</ref> On January 28, 2015, Childress was ruled out for the rest of the season after scans revealed he required surgery for a torn pectoral muscle.<ref>[http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/sydney-kings-lose-star-import-josh-childress-to-seasonending-injury-20150128-12zzq6.html Sydney Kings lose star import Josh Childress to season-ending injury]</ref> In 18 games for the Kings in 2014–15, he averaged 21.1 points, 9.2 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 2.1 blocks per game.<ref>[http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?client=0-189-88249-327335-19755569&sID=&action=PSTATS&pID=198791959 Player statistics for Josh Childress]</ref>

==== 2015–16 season ====
On July 2, 2015, Childress re-signed with the Kings for the [[2015–16 NBL season]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/nbl-team-news/childress-remains-a-king-2/ |title=Childress remains a King |access-date=August 6, 2015 |archive-date=January 9, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109234738/http://www.nbl.com.au/nbl-team-news/childress-remains-a-king-2/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> After missing the first four games of the season with a foot injury, Childress returned to the court on October 23 against the Adelaide 36ers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/injury-update-childress-return/ |title=INJURY UPDATE – CHILDRESS RETURN |access-date=2015-10-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025211706/http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/injury-update-childress-return/ |archive-date=2015-10-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, in his return game, he sustained another injury, this time breaking his right hand. He played through the Kings' 91–80 loss to the 36ers with the break and still managed to score 23 points,<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Childress breaks hand in comeback game for Sydney Kings |date=2015-10-23 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808122748/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-breaks-hand-in-comeback-game-for-sydney-kings-20151023-gkhenx.html |archive-date=2020-08-08 |url-status=live |url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-breaks-hand-in-comeback-game-for-sydney-kings-20151023-gkhenx.html}}</ref> but following the game, he was ruled out for a further four to six games with a [[boxer's fracture]].<ref>[http://www.bordermail.com.au/story/3444864/josh-childress-shattered-by-latest-injury-as-sydney-kings-nbl-struggles-deepen/ Josh Childress shattered by latest injury as Sydney Kings' NBL struggles deepen]</ref> He was subsequently replaced in the line-up by fellow former NBA player [[Al Harrington]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-nba-replacement/ |title=KINGS SIGN NBA REPLACEMENT |access-date=2015-10-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101004138/http://www.sydneykings.com/team-news/kings-sign-nba-replacement/ |archive-date=2015-11-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On November 10, he was suspended for two games for demonstrating unsportsmanlike behaviour on the sidelines during the Kings' loss to the Adelaide 36ers three days prior. Not playing in the game due to his hand injury, Childress verbally abused the referees in the tunnel of [[Titanium Security Arena]] following the conclusion of the match, further tarnishing his reputation in the NBL.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/childress-found-guilty-by-tribunal/ |title=CHILDRESS FOUND GUILTY BY TRIBUNAL |access-date=November 10, 2015 |archive-date=November 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151112130708/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/childress-found-guilty-by-tribunal/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> A third injury to Childress, this time a fractured left hand, was sustained on December 4 against the Cairns Taipans, just two games back after recovering from his previous injury. He was subsequently ruled out for another two to four weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Childress injured again as Cairns Taipans put bite on Sydney Kings  |date=2015-12-04 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414025136/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-injured-again-as-cairns-taipans-put-bite-on-sydney-kings-20151204-glg405.html |archive-date=2021-04-14 |url-status=live |url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-injured-again-as-cairns-taipans-put-bite-on-sydney-kings-20151204-glg405.html}}</ref><ref>[http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/sydney-kings-searching-for-shortterm-replacement-for-josh-childress-20151206-glgneb.html Sydney Kings searching for short-term replacement for Josh Childress]</ref> He was reactivated once again on December 29<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Childress to return for Sydney Kings as Damion James taken off roster |date=2015-12-29 |website=[[The Age]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812214806/https://www.theage.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-to-return-for-sydney-kings-as-damion-james-taken-off-roster-20151229-glwbuj.html |archive-date=2020-08-12 |url-status=live |url=http://www.theage.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-childress-to-return-for-sydney-kings-as-damion-james-taken-off-roster-20151229-glwbuj.html}}</ref> and played out the rest of the season. In 13 games for the last-placed Kings in 2015–16, Childress averaged 21.0 points, 7.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.7 blocks per game.

===Texas Legends (2016)===
On March 8, 2016, Childress was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Texas Legends Acquire NBA Vet Josh Childress|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/texas-legends-acquire-josh-childress/|date=March 8, 2016|access-date=March 8, 2016|work=NBA.com|archive-date=March 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309105008/http://dleague.nba.com/news/texas-legends-acquire-josh-childress/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the Legends in a 115–113 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], recording 17 points, seven rebounds and three blocks in 29 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite news|title=Vipers Edge Legends|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160311/RGVTEX/|date=March 11, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016|work=NBA.com|archive-date=March 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313115847/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160311/RGVTEX/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In eight games for the Legends, he averaged 12.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.0 steals per game.

=== San-en NeoPhoenix (2016–2017) ===
In November 2016, Childress signed with [[San-en NeoPhoenix]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>[http://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/469648/Josh-Childress-is-a-newcomer-at-Sanen Josh Childress is a newcomer at Sanen]</ref> In 40 games, he averaged 18.9 points, 9.5 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.2 blocks per game.

=== Adelaide 36ers (2017–2018) ===
After spending preseason with the [[Denver Nuggets]], Childress signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] for the rest of the [[2017–18 NBL season]] on October 21, 2017, returning to the NBL for a second stint.<ref>[http://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/article/35553-36ers-secure-nba-veteran-josh-childress 36ers secure NBA veteran Josh Childress]</ref><ref>[https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/adelaide-36ers-sign-former-nba-veteran-josh-childress/news-story/64b79c925d92236fed29dbadecd23bf6 Adelaide 36ers sign former NBA veteran Josh Childress]</ref> He helped the 36ers reach the 2018 NBL Grand Final series, where in Game 2, he suffered a shoulder injury that ruled him out for the rest of the series.<ref>[http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/adelaide-36ers-star-josh-childress-to-miss-rest-of-the-nbl-grand-final-series-with-a-broken-shoulder/news-story/624ef4ab7e47801f7bcc741ebdacbdbb Adelaide 36ers star Josh Childress to miss rest of the NBL grand final series with a broken shoulder]</ref> The 36ers went on to lose the grand final series 3–2. In 27 games, he averaged 12.5 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game.

=== Return to the NeoPhoenix (2018–2019) ===
On December 13, 2018, Childress was reported to have signed with [[San-en NeoPhoenix]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=San-en welcomes back Josh Childress|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/557805/San-en-welcomes-back-Josh-Childress|date=December 13, 2018|work=asia-basket.com|access-date=December 13, 2018}}</ref>

==International career==
In 2000, Childress earned a silver medal as a member of the 2000 USA Basketball Men's Youth Development Festival West Team. He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2003 Pan American Games|2003 Pan American Games]].

==Personal==
Childress is featured on the box cover of ''[[ESPN College Hoops 2K5]]'' for the [[PlayStation 2]], published by [[Sega]]. Childress had a high school GPA of 3.5 and scored 1110 on the SAT.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/recruiting/news/2000/07/10/childress_feature/ |work=SI.com |title=Smooth Childress reminiscent of some classics |date=July 10, 2000 |access-date=May 7, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080111052703/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/recruiting/news/2000/07/10/childress_feature/ |archive-date=January 11, 2008 }}</ref> After being waived by the Nets, Childress enrolled back in Stanford and graduated with a degree in [[sociology]] in August 2013.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/josh-childress-back-in-game-after-going-back-to-school/2013/10/07/1537511c-2f55-11e3-9ddd-bdd3022f66ee_story.html | title=Wizards basketball: Josh Childress back in game after going back to school | newspaper=The Washington Post | date=October 7, 2013 | access-date=July 23, 2016 | author=Lee, Michael}}</ref>
